paper_title: Efficient Vision-Language Models for Scientific Figure Parsing
paper_text: Abstract. We benchmark open-weight vision-language models on the task of parsing scientific figures into structured data, a bottleneck that consumes an estimated 3-5 hours per literature review. We introduce SciFig-Bench, a curated set of 1,200 figures from arXiv preprints across physics, biology, and ML, and evaluate four frontier models. Kimi K2.7 achieves the highest accuracy (91.2%) but at the cost of higher latency (340 ms), while GLM 5.2 offers the best latency-accuracy trade-off at 88.7% accuracy and 210 ms. We find that figure-parsing accuracy correlates more strongly with vision pretraining data volume than with total parameter count. Our results suggest that dedicated figure-extraction pipelines can reduce literature-review time by roughly 60%. Prior work by Smith et al. (2024) established that structured figure extraction improves downstream retrieval, and Chen & Patel (2025) showed multimodal models match human accuracy on chart reading, motivating our cross-domain benchmark.
